evals.name: props-destructure-debug

assertions.text: Identifies that destructuring `props` breaks reactivity in Solid
Explains that `props` is a reactive proxy and per-property access is the reactive read
Provides a corrected component that reads `props.name` directly inside JSX (not destructured)

evals.name: for-vs-index
evals.prompt: I have a Solid app with a list of input fields. The user can add and remove fields, and the order is stable (no reordering). Every keystroke causes the entire list to re-render and I lose focus on the active input. Should I use <For> or <Index>? Show me the fix.

assertions.text: Explains that <For> keys by reference (recreates on every value change for primitives) while <Index> keys by position
Notes that with <Index>, the item is a signal (call as item()) rather than a value

evals.name: router-data-fetch
evals.prompt: I'm building a SolidJS app with @solidjs/router. I need a /users/:id route that fetches the user from a server function and shows it. I want: route preloading on hover, automatic deduplication of the fetch, an error boundary with a retry button, and a loading state while pending. Show me the complete route file.

assertions.text: Uses `query(fn, name)` to wrap the fetcher (provides dedup + revalidation)
Uses `createAsync(() => query(args))` to read the data in the component
Exports a route definition with `preload` so hover/focus preload works
Wraps content in <Suspense> with a loading fallback
Wraps content in <ErrorBoundary> whose fallback offers a retry/reset
